title: Bench evidence bundles and cohort replay orchestrator
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Create an orchestrator and on-disk evidence bundle format to capture everything needed to reproduce and triage throughput and latency regressions observed in benchmarks and load tests. The goal is a single-click path from a comparison anomaly in the UI to a reproducible cohort replay that includes request traces, per-token timing, server-side KV cache state snapshots, model binary and kernel selection metadata, hardware allocation (instance IDs), and the exact prompt/seed/temperature used. This ticket spans storage schema, a lightweight replay harness for e2e deterministic playback, and UI hooks that surface an "Open evidence bundle" flow for SRE/bench engineers.
acceptance_criteria: Evidence bundle schema (v1) defined and documented in Confluence with fields for trace, perf histograms, KV snapshot link, model artifact hash, kernel profile, instance metadata, and git commit ID of runtime.
Backend endpoint to create evidence bundles from comparison UI anomalies and store them in the benchmark result store with 30-day retention; bundles must be addressable by bundle_id.
Replay harness that can consume a bundle_id and run a deterministic load profile locally or in a dev cluster reproducing p50/p95 token timings within +/-10% of original run for small cohorts.
UI button in comparison view to attach bundle_id to a case and launch the replay panel with links to trace viewer, per-token waterfall, and a generated suspect-commit hint.
Playbook documenting triage steps, fallbacks, and who to page for infra vs runtime vs model regressions.
Automated smoke test that creates a synthetic anomaly, bundles evidence, replays it, and validates that replay log contains the expected fingerprint.
work_items: Design evidence bundle JSON schema and storage layout (S3 key pattern + RBAC).
Extend benchmark-result ingestion pipeline to emit bundle artifacts when anomaly threshold crossed or "capture" triggered manually.
Implement lightweight deterministic replay harness (python CLI) that can replay requests with recorded timestamps and assert p95 variance.
Add backend API to list and fetch bundles; wire to comparison UI and investigation canvas.
Create UI affordance: 'Create Evidence Bundle' and 'Replay' controls plus a compact bundle inspector tab.
Add unit/integration tests and a CI job that validates bundle roundtrip on PRs affecting ingestion or replay codepaths.
Write runbook and add initial on-call rotations that own triage for first 30 days after launch.
risks: Bundles may contain sensitive prompt data; need redaction policy and KMS encryption at rest.
Deterministic replay may diverge because of non-deterministic kernels, quantization nondeterminism, or downstream service timing.
Storing full traces could increase storage costs if retention not tuned; need sampling or TTL policies.
Large bundles could slow UI; must implement lazy fetch and preview thumbnails.
notes: Initial spike showed we can capture KV cache state for decoder-only models by serializing KV pages per-layer; still need to confirm memory footprint on 32k context runs.
Decision: start with CPU-based deterministic replay for small cohorts (<100 concurrent requests) and a later opt-in GPU-backed replay for larger scale.
PM asked to include a "shareable bundle link" for external partner investigations; this is gated behind enterprise RBAC and will be a follow-up.
